clue.text: Outstanding achievement the new market stores

indicators.note: new tells the solver to make something fresh out of the letters of market stores, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A shop chain's new branch is hailed as a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for MARKET STORES; 'the' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant, decisive move or feat is called a stroke of genius, a supreme stroke.

clue.text: A man accompanying one will get the aperitif

parts.note: Martin is a man's name, any man
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Bring a man along with one and he'll be served a pre-dinner drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanying' just sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth cocktail is a classic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Dreadful pest not allowed to speed

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the word pest is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ball or a player ruled not allowed is out

explanation.surface: An awful nuisance is banned from racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges PEST to STEP; OUT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk briskly is to stride along, to hurry.

clue.text: The Cockney is only a quarter as vulnerable

parts.note: east is one of the four compass quarters, abbreviated E
tender means sore, easily hurt

explanation.surface: A Londoner is said to be a mere fraction as sensitive as others.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End of London. AS is taken as written; 'is only' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney traditionally lives in London's eastern districts, so is a resident of that part of the city.

clue.text: Oceans providing a home for many animals

indicators.note: a home for something holds it inside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: oceans are seas
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: The seas are where countless creatures live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oceans' and 'animals' sit naturally together, hiding that L for 'many' goes inside SEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine mammals with flippers are one kind of animal.

clue.text: Left, so dress in red

indicators.note: in places the word for dress within the word red

parts.note: taken as written
to tire is an old word for to attire, to dress

explanation.surface: Someone departed, so put on scarlet clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRE, an archaic verb meaning to clothe (as in attire), goes inside RED; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has withdrawn from work or from company has gone away.

clue.text: Bovine creatures holding writing up can end relations

indicators.note: holding means the cattle word keeps another piece within it

parts.note: kine is an old plural of cow

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word can

explanation.surface: Cattle carrying documents somehow finish off family ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MS into SM, which goes inside KINE; 'end' adds the last letter of 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: Male relatives by blood are family members.

clue.text: Relief might well be shown as the fans slunk off

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or out of order, so the letters of the fans slunk are rearranged

explanation.surface: Supporters creeping away from a dire match feel glad it is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of THE FANS SLUNK; 'might well be shown as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratitude at escaping trouble is a feeling of ease and release.

clue.text: Tackle little beasts around the North-and the South

indicators.note: around says the animals go round the compass letter

parts.note: hares are small animals
N is the abbreviation for north
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Small animals are rigged with gear across the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside HARES and S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is gear, and the straps on a horse or climber are such equipment.

clue.text: Reverse, but reverse not in any large number

indicators.note: in places the turned word within the word any

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the second reverse tells us to read the word not backwards

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Turn things round, but don't turn round in great numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'reverse' turns NOT into TON, which goes 'in' ANY; M follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the opposite meaning is the converse of another.

clue.text: Distort twisted miser here and now

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of miser are bent into a new order

parts.note: something here and now is present

explanation.surface: A warped skinflint is around right now to bend the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges MISER as MISRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a false account of something is to twist it.

clue.text: It's really offensive, so no one will take part

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
some means a part, a portion

explanation.surface: Something so nasty that nobody will join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' and 'will take' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A foul-smelling, repellent thing is disgusting.

clue.text: Saves the boat being filled by wave

indicators.note: being filled by says the boat holds the next piece inside

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to crimp hair is to wave it

explanation.surface: A vessel is swamped by a breaker.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIMP, to put waves in hair, goes inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise stingily is to put money by.

clue.text: Dishonestly get rid of the duck in hand

indicators.note: in puts the duck inside the hand

parts.note: a closed hand is a fist
a duck is a cricket score of nought, O

explanation.surface: Someone cheatingly offloads a bird they are holding.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, so O.
explanation.definitionFit: To palm off something unwanted on another person by deceit.

clue.text: Last month the civil engineer would accept port-or decline

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, DEC
Aden is a port in Yemen
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: In December the engineer took on a harbour job, or turned it down.
explanation.walkthrough: ADEN goes inside CE after DEC; 'or' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral or cultural falling-off is a decay, a degeneration.

clue.text: Glad to accommodate trendy moderate

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the word for glad holds the other inside

parts.note: content means pleased, glad
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Happy to make room for a fashionable but restrained person.
explanation.walkthrough: IN goes inside CONTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing self-restraint, especially in appetite, means being temperate.

clue.text: See a female given cunningly-fashioned ring in opera

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, see
a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: cunningly fashioned says the word ring is reworked into another shape

explanation.surface: Watch a woman receive a craftily made ring at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly-fashioned' rearranges RING to GRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's work about the swan knight is one stage work set to music.

clue.text: Having worked at the garden, now maybe give a party

parts.note: hoed means having worked the soil with a hoe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word now is only one possible order of its letters

explanation.surface: After gardening, someone might throw a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges NOW to OWN; 'give' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively social gathering with folk dancing is a type of social event.

clue.text: Slight oversight

explanation.surface: A small mistake made by not watching.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to slight or disregard, and as a noun a failure to attend, a lapse.

clue.text: Control is always shown by a good man

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good man
e'er is a poetic form of ever, always

explanation.surface: Discipline is something a decent fellow always displays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'shown by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide or direct something is to have it under command.

clue.text: There's drink left-keep up!

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: There's still some booze, so carry on!
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something up or bear its weight is to prop it.

clue.text: Sickening preparations

parts.note: read sickening as making someone vomit, and preparations as medicines a pharmacist makes up

explanation.surface: Revolting arrangements made in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sickening' looks like disgusting, but here it literally means causing sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs given to induce vomiting are medicines that make patients throw up.

clue.text: Stand to set a record on unfamiliar green

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: unfamiliar suggests green is not in its usual form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bid to set a world record on a strange golf green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfamiliar' rearranges GREEN to ERGNE; 'to set' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental table centrepiece with dishes is a decorative holder.

clue.text: Some of the men don't get any better

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain men never improve.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through thE MEN Don't.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or improve a text is to make it better.

clue.text: Print what the reporter might say

explanation.surface: Stamp what a journalist would announce.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M PRESS, it is a journalist introducing themself.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp a mark is to print it, and a reporter could declare being a member of the newspaper trade.

clue.text: An alien in Britain nowadays needs love-never more so…

annotationWithheld.why: An alien in Britain nowadays needs love-never more so… (7): no parse found for S + LOVE + NE from 'needs love-never more so'; the wordplay cannot be explained honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: An alien in Britain nowadays needs love-never more so…

clue.text: … but the god of love, in encompassing love, can be wearing

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the word in goes round the letter for love

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: But the god of love, wrapped in love, may prove tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside IN to make ION after EROS; 'but' and 'can be' link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradual wearing away of rock or soil is attrition.

clue.text: Test a sun and diet treatment in the country

indicators.note: treatment means the letters of the phrase are processed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A trial of sun and diet therapy in rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' signals an anagram of TEST A SUN plus DIET; 'and' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a nation, a federal country.
